name: Deepgram
intro: Deepgram has sold speech-to-text APIs to enterprises for a decade without ever publishing a revenue figure — it is carried here at an estimated ~$50M+ threshold, corroborated by a $1.3B Series C valuation in January 2026 and 1,300+ enterprise customers. The timeline below mixes funding milestones with clearly flagged third-party estimates.

modelTitle: How Voice APIs Bill by the Second.
modelParagraphs: Deepgram monetizes a speech AI platform on usage-based API pricing: per-minute or per-character rates for speech-to-text (including real-time streaming), text-to-speech and voice-agent APIs, with enterprise contracts layered on top for volume commitments, on-prem or VPC deployments and SLAs. Customers span voice-agent builders like Vapi and productivity tools like Granola — infrastructure that bills by the audio second.

The January 2026 Series C doubled down on the 'voice AI economy' thesis: acquiring YC-backed OfOne for real-time voice automation, and pointing at the $14–20B voice AI market growing roughly 30% a year. Because revenue tracks minutes transcribed rather than seats, Deepgram's top line compounds with its customers' call volume — the classic infrastructure revenue pattern.

faqs.a: Deepgram has not precisely disclosed its ARR. It is carried here at an estimated ~$50 million threshold, consistent with third-party research; the hard public anchors are a $1.3 billion valuation from a $130 million Series C in January 2026 and 1,300+ enterprise customers.

faqs.q: Why Is Deepgram's Revenue Only an Estimate?
faqs.a: The company has never published revenue figures. Its funding milestones — $72M Series B in 2022 and $130M Series C at $1.3B in January 2026 — plus customer counts are the primary public signals used to frame the estimate.

Usage-based API pricing for speech-to-text, text-to-speech and voice-agent infrastructure — billed per minute or per character — plus enterprise contracts with volume commitments and private deployments. Revenue scales with customers' audio volume, not seat counts.

$1.3 billion after a $130 million Series C led by AVP in January 2026, with participation from In-Q-Tel, Madrona, Tiger Global, Wing and Y Combinator. Total funding is roughly $220 million since the 2017 Y Combinator seed.

1,300+ enterprises, including voice-agent platforms like Vapi and AI notetaker Granola, with over 2,000 products described as 'Powered by Deepgram' at the time of the Series C. It targets the $14–20B voice AI market growing roughly 30% annually.
